title: Secondary Injection into Remote Shells and Utilities
platform_conditions: POSIX sh and bash on Linux/macOS; ssh invokes the remote user's login shell to parse the command string, so quoting semantics on the remote side follow the remote account's shell
security_mechanism: A remote command given as one quoted string is parsed twice: the local shell expands $x first, then ssh hands the resulting string to the remote user's login shell, which parses it again as shell grammar. A value containing a space, semicolon, quote or $ therefore changes meaning between the two parses — an attacker-controlled filename like 'a; rm -rf /' executes on the remote host as a second command. The same double-parse exists in program-text injection: sed 's/.../$x/' and awk scripts interpolate input into the program source, an unquoted here-doc delimiter lets the remote/local body expand $vars, and concatenating input into SQL, JSON, or python -c payloads re-uses the host string as target-language syntax.

source_sink_clues.source: Values crossing an interpreter boundary: filenames and hostnames fed into ssh commands, log fields or user text fed into sed/awk programs, form input concatenated into SQL/JSON bodies, and arguments to python -c / psql -c style invocations.
source_sink_clues.sink: ssh host "...$var..."; sed/awk invocations with interpolated program text; here-docs whose delimiter is unquoted; string concatenation into SQL statements, JSON payloads, or python -c/- <<EOF script bodies

tracking_guards: Check values crossing to a remote shell are single-quoted with printf '%q' (or quoted with ' careful escaping) so the local expansion produces one literal remote operand; check sed/awk receive data via -v or ENVIRON/stdin rather than string substitution into the program; check here-doc delimiters are quoted ('EOF') to suppress expansion; check SQL/JSON/python -c bodies are built from structured encoders, not concatenation.
not_candidate_when: The remote command is a fixed string and no local variable is interpolated, the interpolated value is passed with printf '%q' quoting so it arrives as one literal remote operand, the here-doc delimiter is quoted and the body is constant, or program text for sed/awk/SQL is constant with data supplied through separate data channels.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html
